topics.title: The hawk at rest: the top of the wood

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the hawk's position and stillness as it sits with closed eyes at the top of the wood.
Explain how the hawk sees the trees, the air, the sun and the earth as existing for its advantage.

topics.title: Physical prowess and 'Creation in my foot'

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the hawk's physical features (hooked head, hooked feet, locked feet, feathers) and their significance.
Interpret the claim that Creation produced the hawk and that it now holds Creation in its foot.

topics.title: Violence, frankness and the allotment of death

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse the images of killing that present the hawk's absolute, unquestioned power.
Explain what the hawk means by 'no sophistry in my body' and 'No arguments assert my right'.
Interpret the hawk's claim that nothing has changed and that it will keep things like this.
Evaluate the parallel the poem suggests between the hawk's predatory arrogance and human tyranny.

topics.title: The poet, the monologue form and the language

concepts.learning_objective: Recall key facts about Ted Hughes and the qualities of his animal poems.
Identify the poem as a monologue spoken by the hawk and explain the effect of this form and the title.
Infer the meanings of words such as 'buoyancy' and 'roosting' in the context of the poem.
